messages.content: Private page. Nobody gets this, including me if I can help it. I'm 33, night shift over, I locked the staff toilet, I did not cry, I made a joke at bed 4 that was for me. Pink soap. Badge still on. No lesson at the end.

<think>
First person, ugly, stop before a moral.
[frame: pathway=s1|mode=chat|construct=diary|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
</think>

I made the joke and then I came in here and locked the door like the joke might follow me. I did not cry. The soap is the pink kind that smells like nothing and my badge is still clipped, biting. If I write what I learned I will be writing for the charge nurse, so I won't. The joke was mine. That's the worst part and the only part.
Write tonight as me, 28, at the kitchen table. I deleted four openings. The only true thing is a bucket someone drummed on at the picket. No one will read this. Don't make it brave.

I deleted the magazine four times and the bucket is still in my head like a rude guest. I was there. I am not brave about it on this page. The mug is cold. If I add a moral I'll sand the bucket into a point, and the point will be for Paul. Paul is not invited. The bucket stays. I don't even like drums.
Private. I'm 41. I sit in the car twenty minutes before I go inside. Don't explain me to an audience.
Twenty minutes again. The engine's off so I can't pretend it's the drive. I know what's inside. I still sit here like the seat is a decision I haven't lost yet.
Add the part where I check the work chat and then don't go in.

I opened the chat, saw the invoice thread, and put the phone face down on the passenger seat like it had accused me. Then I sat longer. I am not proud of the arithmetic. I am also not turning this into growth. The house lights are on. I'm still out here.
After the hearing. I'm 62. The two dates are in the folder. I almost gave a speech and didn't. Private page.

I kept the speech in my mouth and put the two dates on the table instead. My hands shook anyway. The 3rd and the 9th did the work. I wanted to be moving and I was only clear. That's enough for a page no one will congratulate.
End it with what this taught me about courage.
It taught me nothing I will write down for an audience, and this page is not about to become one. The dates, the shake, the speech I didn't spend. Stop.
Ask me questions. I delete every first line. Don't write the paragraph.

Whose voice are you deleting?

What did you see that you won't put first?
Stop asking. Write the page as me, private, 28, the bucket, the deletions, no one else in the room.

I deleted four lines that sounded like a magazine and the bucket is still the thing I won't dignify by using it. I was at the picket. The mug is cold. This page doesn't get a turn. I don't want to be good at this tonight. The bucket can sit here without becoming a symbol, which is more than I gave it all evening.
